_readme: The complete set of NON-APP-SPECIFIC screens: the ones that are the same in all fifty apps and
therefore ship in the chassis rather than being written per app. Sourced from DoD §4-A.
WHY A REGISTER AND NOT A CHECKLIST IN PROSE. C-13's acceptance is that a NAMED LIST is declared and
the app_brick probe asserts each screen is present in a fresh stamp. A list nobody can check is how
an account-deletion button sat doing nothing for months while passing every check the repo had.
present  - it exists in the chassis; `anchor` names the file and the symbol that prove it
blocked  - it CANNOT be built yet; `blockedBy` names what has to land first, and that claim is
checked (a blocker that has already shipped fails the build, so nothing hides behind
todo     - buildable now, not yet built. Counted and PRINTED on every run.
ANCHOR KINDS. `anchor.kind` says what the symbol IS, because a bare word match is the
declaration-vs-usage trap: renaming `class NotFoundScreen` to `class NotFoundScreenGone` left the
guard green, since the class's own constructor still matched the bare name.
class  (default) - our own widget/class; matches the DECLARATION
uses             - a Flutter widget we use rather than declare (SegmentedButton, AboutListTile)

screens.what: A friendly screen when a widget throws during build, instead of Flutter's grey/red default.

reachable.why: installed before runApp, so an error in the FIRST build is already covered

screens.what: 404 for a route that does not resolve. Matters most on web, where a user can type a URL or follow a stale link.

reachable.why: without it go_router shows its own error page, which names internal route patterns

screens.what: Tells the user the network could not be reached. Driven by a FAILED REQUEST, not a connectivity plugin — knowing the radio is on says nothing about whether the API is reachable.
The kill-switch wall when the running version is below min_supported_version.

reachable.why: mounted in MaterialApp's builder, above the router

screens.what: The DPDP analytics consent question. THE single piece that turns the whole analytics rail on.

reachable.why: [2]C-6: the recorder had ZERO call sites and every event was silently discarded, and no test went red because refusing is the correct behaviour when consent is absent
a screen no route reaches is one no user can open

screens.what: Opens a support email with the app name pre-filled.
Delete the account and its data, with re-authentication first.

reachable.why: its confirm button called Navigator.pop and NOTHING else until 2026-07-28 — a store-compliance defect that passed every check the repo had

screens.what: Standard about dialog with version and legalese.

screens.detail: PaywallGate exists in the design system with ZERO consumers. Wiring it before a payment can be taken would be a fail-closed seam with no proven open path — the [2]C-6 shape. Kept as a shell deliberately.
Nothing can be purchased yet, so every one of these would be a screen no path reaches.

screens.what: Sign-in, sign-up and forgot-password, plus the redirect guard that gates every other route.

reachable.why: the REDIRECT GUARD is what makes these screens reachable — screens do not navigate after sign-in themselves, because pushing from both places leaves two routes racing to be top of the stack

screens.what: Password reset, email verification and the OAuth callback — the screens a link outside the app lands on.
screens.detail: Each of these is entered by following a link from an EMAIL or a browser redirect, so none can be reached without deep-link handling. `app_links` 7.2.1 supports all six platforms (verified against pub.dev 2026-07-28) and would earn its place under [2]C-4 as native-binary — it ships platform code — but it is not a dependency yet. ⚠️ Web carries two traps recorded in AuthCapabilities: the token arrives in the URL FRAGMENT so query parsing fails SILENTLY, and app_links on web reports only the INITIAL link.
Buildable now — no dependency on auth or money.

screens.what: Profile / notification prefs / language / privacy-export / legal / sign-out.
screens.detail: Sign-out is buildable now that [2]C-15 landed. Privacy-export needs the subly-api EXPORTS R2 binding, which is bound and used NOWHERE — routed to stage 4.

screens.what: Ask for a store review at a good moment.
screens.detail: Needs in_app_review, which under [2]C-4 lands in platform_storage rather than earning its own package.
